purpose: 14 high-risk papal, thematic, typological and saint-feast paintings after first four direct-scene batches
method: Institutional museum catalogue, exact-object evidence, 2026 Roman Missal reading cross-check and identified photo/uploader separation; no raw image pixel inspection
rules: Historical user placement/subject approvals are unchanged; no independent auto assignment
Do not conflate historical artist, image photographer or uploader
Do not collapse multiple physical artworks with similar subject names without exact identifier verification
Hold St Damasus Gospel as competing formulary readings until rubric/source selection reconciled
Do not claim a saint feast painting illustrates a Mass Gospel when it represents a different event
Typological, liturgical, devotional and thematic matches may be valuable without being exact narrative depictions
Photograph licensing, exact bytes, quality, crop and mobile review are independent of match relevance

records.artwork_title: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter
records.claude_scripture_source: Christ giving the keys to Peter fits the papal common Gospel, Matthew 16:13–19; there is no portrait of Marcellus I.
records.object_identity: NGA accession 1958.8.105; Lorenzo Monaco miniature on vellum
records.findings: The proposed Keys scene (Matthew 16:13–19) does not illustrate this day's Matthew 16:24–27 self-denial Gospel. It remains a Petrine succession visual, not a St Marcellus portrait or exact pericope. The painting record is a miniature on vellum, not an oil painting.

records.artwork_title: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter
records.claude_scripture_source: Christ giving the keys fits the papal Gospel; there is no portrait of Soter or Caius.
records.findings: Claude's target scripture Matthew 16:13–19 conflicts with 1962 Sts Soter and Caius common Gospel John 15:5–11 (vine and branches). The Keys image remains only a wider papal subject match.

records.artwork_title: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter
records.claude_scripture_source: Christ giving the keys fits the papal Gospel; there is no portrait of Callistus.
records.findings: The papal feast's Matthew 16:13–19 Gospel depicts keys of Peter. Suitable exact-Gospel and papal theological association, but no depiction of Callistus I and no placement-level owner lock inferred.

records.artwork_title: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter
records.claude_scripture_source: Christ giving the keys fits the papal Gospel; there is no portrait of Martin I.
records.findings: St Martin I 1962 Gospel Luke 14:26–33 concerns radical discipleship; the Keys illumination is a general papal image only. No historical St Martin portrait.

records.artwork_title: Christ Giving the Keys to Saint Peter
records.claude_scripture_source: Christ giving the keys fits the papal Gospel; there is no portrait of Damasus.
records.findings: Two 1962 sources disagree on the St Damasus Mass: FSSPX Ordo uses Matt 24:42–47 and LatinMassPropers gives Matt 16:13–19. Preserve source plurality and investigate which formularies/rubrical variants apply; never overwrite the user's existing Calendar Gospel with unadjudicated single-source inference.

records.artwork_title: Suffer the Little Children come to Me
records.claude_scripture_source: De Vriendt's 'Suffer the little children' echoes Bosco's mission to the young (Matthew 18:1–5 is a related passage, not the same episode).
records.verified_or_disputed_gospel: Matthew 18:1–5 [Claude's contextual passage; exact Mass Gospel not independently checked]
records.object_identity: Commons source photographic candidate, physical collection not identified in this batch
records.findings: Christ and children relates to St John Bosco's mission to youth only by theological/charitable analogy. Neither a representation of Bosco himself nor automatically an exact Gospel scene for his feast. Physical-object inventory pending.

records.claude_scripture_source: Reni's Immaculate Conception (legacy approved) answers the Lourdes title 'I am the Immaculate Conception'.
records.object_identity: Metropolitan Museum of Art accession 59.32 / object 437423
records.findings: Reni's Immaculate Conception represents Marian doctrine and resonates with Lourdes declaration 'I am the Immaculate Conception', but does not portray the 1858 Lourdes apparition. Remains a valid alternative theological connection, not date primary by default.

records.claude_scripture_source: Isenbrandt's Mother of Seven Sorrows matches the Servite charism, without reusing the protected Seven Sorrows cover.
records.object_identity: Musea Brugge source painting (exact inv not separately checked)
records.findings: Our Lady of Seven Sorrows embodies the Order of Servants of Mary's devotion, but does not depict the seven 13th-century founders. Must not classify as founding narrative or literal founder portrait.

records.corrected_or_qualified_artist_credit: Paul Bril (older Joconde); present Lille catalogue: entourage de Paul Bril
records.claude_scripture_source: Bril's Shipwreck of Jonah is the 'sign of Jonah' Christ cites in Matthew 12:38–41: an Old Testament type, not the Gospel scene.
records.object_identity: Lille Palais des Beaux-Arts, government Joconde P 1904 vs current museum website inventory 976.3.1; identify alias or different object before canonising
records.findings: Gospel invokes sign of Jonah (Matthew 12), justifying theological typology. Sources disagree on inventory number and attribution: older Joconde 'P 1904' and 'Paul Bril'; current Lille museum labels '976.3.1' and 'circle of Paul Bril'. Do not assert these are same object without accession/photo proof. RMN photography restricted.

records.claude_scripture_source: Honthorst's Christ before the High Priest is the later trial, not the council's deliberation in John 11:47–54.
records.object_identity: Gerard van Honthorst Christ Before the High Priest, Commons candidate
records.findings: John 11:47–54 records a council planning the death of Jesus before His arrest; Honthorst's later trial before the High Priest is a different historical episode. Merely anticipatory Passion context, not literal Gospel.

records.artwork_title: Augustins - Martirio di San Giovanni e San Paolo - Giovanni Francesco Barbieri, Il Guercin
records.corrected_or_qualified_artist_credit: Giovanni Francesco Barbieri (Guercino), NOT Commons photographer Didier Descouens
records.claude_scripture_source: The Martyrdom of Saints John and Paul (Barbieri/Guercino, Toulouse) depicts the Roman martyrs of the feast.
records.findings: The attributed painter is Guercino; Claude's Didier Descouens is uploader/photographer. Work title says Martyrdom of Saints John and Paul, but a French institutional subject keyword lists 'saint Paul de Tarse'; distinguish feast's Roman martyrs from apostles and verify iconography before exact feast identification.

records.observance: Dedication of the Basilica of St. Mary Major
records.claude_scripture_source: The Cretan Glycophilousa icon recalls the Byzantine Marian icon tradition of Santa Maria Maggiore; it is not the Salus Populi Romani itself.
records.object_identity: Musea Paris candidate icon PPP4869, School of Crete
records.findings: Glycophilousa is a Mother of God icon type, but not the specific Salus Populi Romani venerated at Santa Maria Maggiore. Only broad devotional/iconographic relevance for dedication, not an image of the basilica or its icon.

records.corrected_or_qualified_artist_credit: Carlo Sellitto; Edelseider is Commons photographer/uploader, not painter
records.claude_scripture_source: Sellitto's Saint Bruno depicts the saint of the day.
records.object_identity: Strasbourg Musée des Beaux-Arts inv 432 (Commons artwork metadata; institution source not independently fetched in this batch)
records.findings: Claude's artist field 'Edelseider' is a source metadata parsing mistake. The painting in the specific Commons item is credited to Carlo Sellitto, St Bruno. Old attribution Bernardino Cesari reported in source; institutional artist/photo QA remains open.

records.observance: Dedication of the Archbasilica of Our Holy Savior
records.artwork_title: Augustins - Le Pape Urbain II consacrant la Basilique Saint-Sernin de Toulouse - Antoine R
records.corrected_or_qualified_artist_credit: Antoine Rivalz; Didier Descouens is Commons photographer, not painter
records.claude_scripture_source: Pope Urban II consecrating the Basilica of Saint-Sernin depicts a basilica dedication rite; Zacchaeus (Luke 19:1–10) is not among approved works.
records.object_identity: Musée des Augustins Toulouse 2004.1.266, Antoine Rivalz 1715
records.findings: Official French institutional records identify Pope Urban II consecrating Saint-Sernin Toulouse, NOT Lateran Basilica of Our Savior. Luke 19:1–10 is Zacchaeus, also not shown. Qualifies at most as generic depiction of church consecration. Existing owner selections must not be displaced.
